name: Tuvalu

findings.controller: SubCom (cable supplier); Google (Bulikula trunk, Pacific Connect)
findings.local_actor: Tuvalu Telecommunications Corporation (TTC); Government of Tuvalu
findings.builder: SubCom (cable); Google technical partner with subcontractors incl. Ciena
findings.financier: Grant package: Australia (AIFFP, up to USD 37m), Japan, New Zealand, Taiwan, United States (incl. USTDA grant to TTC)
findings.summary: Tuvalu's first international submarine cable, the Vaka cable, branches about 668 km from Funafuti to Google's Bulikula trunk; SubCom supplied the cable, it landed in December 2024 and was launched by TTC in October 2025.

sources.publisher: Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific (AIFFP)
Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific (AIFFP)

findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: SubCom (US) supplied the cable per SubTel Forum, and the onward trunk is Google's, so pole us. SubCom is named only by SubTel Forum; launch is corroborated by DCD, Pacific Island Times and AIFFP. USD 56m is the announced total (SubTel Forum, Pacific Island Times); no audited figure. still_current true from the October 2025 launch. AIFFP groundbreaking page gives no year.

findings.controller: Alepo (LTE core, charging, policy, BSS; Austin, Texas)
findings.summary: State operator TTC selected Alepo's LTE-in-a-box core platform, with charging, policy and BSS, and integrator Blue Arcus to launch LTE and WiFi in Funafuti, upgrading from 3G, targeting service in early 2017.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us from the US-headquartered core vendor; RAN vendor not named in either source. Tier 3 as a vendor selection with counterparty but no value; commercial launch not confirmed by these sources. Total Telecom item is a Blue Arcus press release, so not independent. Pre-2020 and not reconfirmed as current.

research_gaps: Falepili Union (signed 8 May 2024): Article 4(4) requires Tuvalu to mutually agree with Australia any security engagement with third states, and the DFAT explanatory memorandum lists telecommunications as covered critical infrastructure. Not coded as a finding (constraint, not a deployment or reversal); reviewer to decide how to represent it and confirm entry-into-force date.
TTC mobile RAN vendor (LTE sites in Funafuti and outer islands) not established; confirm whether the 2017 Alepo/Blue Arcus LTE core is still in service.
Owner of the Vaka cable asset (Government of Tuvalu vs TTC) and Google's ongoing O&M role; landing-station equipment vendor.
Digital Nation programme (Digital Ark, digital twin, e-government): who hosts the cloud platform and where; no vendor named in the Global Voices report.
Satellite connectivity (e.g. Starlink or Kacific) licensing or bans, not searched.
